question: What is CAC?
headline: CAC: Paid media spend per new customer.
narrative: CAC = total spend divided by total new customers. Ratios are always computed from summed numerators and denominators, never as an average of daily ratios.
How to read it: What it costs to bring in a first-time buyer.
Watch out: Counts only media spend, so it understates the full cost of acquisition.
It is only defined for paid channels, because owned channels carry no media spend in this data.

Driver analysis splits it into: Cost per thousand impressions (CPM); Impressions per click (the inverse of CTR); Clicks per session; Sessions per order (the inverse of conversion rate); Orders per new customer.

question: How does anomaly detection work?
headline: How anomalies are found
narrative: Each daily series is split into trend, weekly pattern and residual with a robust seasonal decomposition. A day is flagged only when its residual is more than 8 robust standard deviations from normal and the value is at least 15% away from what was expected, which keeps false alarms to roughly one every five years per series on clean data. Consecutive flagged days are merged into one incident. Known retail dates such as Black Friday are labelled so they are not mistaken for faults.
